races.name: Town And Country Cakes Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Just Johnny
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran with three recent runs at 2m+ on good ground, all placed out of the frame; this drop back to 1m2f looks a significant trip compression that may catch him cold, and 357 days without a run is a serious fitness concern at age five.|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a bumper at Uttoxeter on his latest start, Just Johnny is returning from a spell on the sidelines and has plenty to prove in this novice company; his preference for being held up means he will need things to fall right.

runners_data.name: Dialstone
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's unexposed three-year-old with no public form available; Beckett's strong 14-day figures (7/57) suggest a yard in form, and lightly-raced status means the ceiling is genuinely unknown — going is a concern only because we have no data.|
runners_data.comment: A Time Test gelding and half-brother to the useful Newbolt, who showed his best at eight furlongs, Dialstone has solid pedigree credentials for this trip with a dam also effective at seven furlongs; he debuts with a trainer who has a strong record at this venue.

runners_data.name: Liberate
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's once-raced filly placed on soft at 1m2f; the step onto faster ground is the key unknown, and 24 days between runs is a workmanlike prep, but form from a single soft-ground run is thin evidence for a competitive restricted novice.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth on his opening start at Lingfield, beaten three lengths, Liberate showed enough ability to make him interesting here and could benefit from racing with more purpose; the current trip may prove on the shorter side in time, but he is capable of progress.

runners_data.name: Mother Dear
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win at 1m2f on good and a recent 38-day break; Hughie Morrison fires two runners here and this one has the cleanest going profile of the field, making her the most likely horse to challenge Egyptian Pharaoh's lead from an organised early position.|
runners_data.comment: A winner in a novice at Goodwood last time by three-quarters of a length, Mother Dear arrives in fine form with connections in good shape, and her middle-distance breeding suggests this longer trip will suit; she is a clear danger to go one better again.

runners_data.name: Adalo
runners_data.note: William Haggas's well-bred three-year-old has run twice on good ground at 1m-1m2f without threatening the frame; a true hold-up horse by style who has been redistributed to midfield on the map — Fallon will likely find himself further back than ideal given how few natural front-runners are in this field to create gaps.|
runners_data.comment: Held at Windsor last time in a novice, Adalo is lightly raced and brings middle-distance breeding that points to substantial improvement ahead; both outings so far have left plenty of room for development and he should step forward considerably from this stage.

runners_data.name: Egyptian Pharaoh
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who shapes the entire race; four runs show consistency without a win, and tongue-tie is applied again, but the ability to dictate on a flat track at a comfortable gallop is a major positional asset that the low OR belies.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent across recent starts including a two-and-a-quarter-length third at Windsor last time, Egyptian Pharaoh handles the distance and going well and is fitted with a first-time tongue-tie; he tops our ratings here and looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Tinkety Tonk
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has been behind in both turf starts, including a tailed-off 12th last time at 1m2f on good — that form is deeply unencouraging, though lightly-raced status and Morrison's yard means a bounce-back cannot be entirely dismissed.|
runners_data.comment: Comfortably held in a maiden at Goodwood last time, Tinkety Tonk showed a minor improvement from his previous effort but remains difficult to recommend with confidence; his trainer is in good form, which provides at least some basis for hope.

runners_data.name: Celestial Cen
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's once-raced runner placed at 1m2f on soft; Pierre-Louis Jamin is a shrewd booking and Watson's 14-day figures (3/35) are fair, but like Liberate the transition to faster ground from a single run is a leap of faith rather than a form-based recommendation.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up on her opening start at Lingfield, beaten just half a length, Celestial Cen showed good raw ability and should come on for the experience; she shapes as a strong danger here, though a quicker break out of the gates could be decisive.

races.paceDynamic: Egyptian Pharaoh is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 1m2f novice and, with no genuine rival looking to contest the lead, Billy Loughnane should be able to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground. Mother Dear is the one prominent horse likely to sit just off the pace, but the remainder of the field — Just Johnny, Adalo, Tinkety Tonk and the lightly-raced trio — are hold-up or unknown-style types who will need to come from behind. The field contains more genuine hold-up horses than the map can place at the rear, with Adalo redistributed to midfield despite being a true hold-up type, meaning its natural position will be contested and it is unlikely to get the clean passage it needs. An uncontested, slow-to-moderate pace on fast ground over a stiff mile-and-a-quarter suits a horse that can travel prominently and has the class to quicken from the front or just off it — the tactical verdict strongly favours the prominent profile, with Egyptian Pharaoh controlling tempo and Mother Dear best placed to exploit any weakness.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Egyptian Pharaoh Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Egyptian Pharaoh bowls along uncontested and sets a steady-to-moderate pace throughout, dictating every yard from the front.
scenarios.body: If Egyptian Pharaoh bowls along uncontested and sets a steady-to-moderate pace throughout, dictating every yard from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late-Closers Benefit From Class
scenarios.trigger: If Egyptian Pharaoh sets a genuinely strong tempo that stretches the field and burns off the prominent runners before the home turn.
scenarios.body: If Egyptian Pharaoh sets a genuinely strong tempo that stretches the field and burns off the prominent runners before the home turn.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Duel Softens Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Mother Dear pushes forward early and applies pressure on Egyptian Pharaoh, creating a genuine contested lead from the outset.
scenarios.body: If Mother Dear pushes forward early and applies pressure on Egyptian Pharaoh, creating a genuine contested lead from the outset.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly-Raced Improver Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unraced or once-raced unexposed types proves significantly better than their debut effort and the modest pace masks their inexperience.
scenarios.body: If one of the unraced or once-raced unexposed types proves significantly better than their debut effort and the modest pace masks their inexperience.

watchPoints.text: Egyptian Pharaoh's ability to control tempo unopposed is the hinge of the entire race — if Loughnane bowls clear at a crawl from the front, every hold-up runner is tactically compromised and cannot produce a winning turn of foot.|

Mother Dear is the one horse with the profile and the form to pressure or track Egyptian Pharaoh; watch whether Rob Hornby elects to sit behind or challenge for the lead, as that decision will determine whether this becomes a contested or uncontested gallop.|

Adalo is a genuine hold-up type placed in midfield on the map — Cieren Fallon will need to manage position carefully in a field of eight where most others also want to come from off the pace, and a lack of racing room late could cost it.|

Three runners (Dialstone, Liberate, Celestial Cen) are lightly raced with unknown form profiles; any of them could land a significant step forward in their second or third career start, making the win market harder to compress around the established runners.|

The going is confirmed Good to Firm at Ffos Las, not Good as listed in the race header — Just Johnny and Mother Dear have established sim-going form, while Liberate and Celestial Cen ran their sole starts on soft, meaning ground suitability splits the field cleanly.|

races.name: West Wales Properties Pembrokeshire Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Dark Whisper
runners_data.note: Consecutive placed finishes at 8f on Good ground give this David Menuisier runner strong form credentials for the conditions; Billy Loughnane rides and the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 4/14 is respectable, making this one of the more reliably profiled horses in the race from a prominent berth.
runners_data.comment: Placed on both career starts, including a three-and-a-half-length third at Nottingham last time, Dark Whisper handles good ground at this distance and has a trainer in good form; every expectation he will improve on those efforts.

runners_data.name: Impierious
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's lightly-raced three-year-old has back-to-back thirds at 8f on Good and arrives 25 days fresh; Kieran O'Neill takes the ride and the horse's unresolved ceiling leaves its ceiling genuinely open, though the lack of a win from two starts suggests a finishing effort rather than a dominant display.
runners_data.comment: Placed third on both outings, including a four-length third at Doncaster last time, Impierious handles the distance and going and is expected to improve further; his consistent form makes him the one to beat in this maiden company.

runners_data.name: Ingemar
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's lightly-raced runner has only one outing to reference — a fifth over 10f on Good — and stepping back to a mile introduces trip uncertainty; Rob Hornby rides but the trainer's 0/11 14-day form is a concern and the horse remains highly unexposed.
runners_data.comment: Beaten on his debut at Doncaster last time, Ingemar left the impression he might benefit from racing closer to the pace and has scope to show better; he remains lightly raced and some improvement from that opening effort is entirely plausible.

runners_data.name: Lean d'Aislingean
runners_data.note: Charlie Pike's hold-up operator has two starts on Soft ground and now faces Good to Firm for the first time, which is a going query worth monitoring; Edward Greatrex rides and the horse's most recent effort was a third over 8f suggesting stamina for this trip, but the slower-paced scenario this race will likely produce is not ideal for a hold-up style.
runners_data.comment: An improved third at Windsor last time, Lean d'Aislingean has stepped forward from his debut and carries middle-distance breeding that suggests he will continue to develop; he looks a strong danger here, though he may be better served by a longer trip in due course.

runners_data.name: Next Guilian
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's runner carries a flag for fading in the finish and has an eighth on Soft ground as its main reference; Darragh Keenan rides and a 22-day turnaround is fine, but the prominent style combined with the tendency to empty late makes this a horse to oppose if the pace quickens at all.
runners_data.comment: Beaten at Windsor last time in line with recent form, Next Guilian has little to recommend him here on current evidence and his previous experience on the continent yielded little of note; softer conditions would suit him better.

runners_data.name: Vincenzo Bellini
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's debutant arrives with no racecourse form on record, leaving going preference, trip aptitude and racing style entirely unknown; Kaiya Fraser rides for a stable with a modest 1/19 14-day return, making this one of the most opaque runners in the field.
runners_data.comment: A 28,000gns breeze-up purchase by Wootton Bassett, Vincenzo Bellini carries the breeding interest of a high-class dam over seven furlongs as a juvenile, which is appealing for this trip on paper; his trainer is currently out of form, which tempers expectations on debut.

runners_data.name: Elenaya
runners_data.note: 192 days off the track is the headline concern here — George Bass rides for the same Mark Loughnane yard and the hold-up style suits the likely pace scenario least; tongue-tie is applied and the best previous effort was a fifth over 7f on Good, making a step up to a mile on a first start since winter a significant ask.
runners_data.comment: Absent for over six months and beaten in both career starts, Elenaya has shown limited form to date and has plenty to prove in this company; first-time tongue-tie is the main change and she needs a significant step up to be competitive here.

runners_data.name: Kino Plasmat
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old is the race's only confirmed front-runner and has a sole start — fourth over 7f on Soft — to work from; Cieren Fallon is a high-quality booking and the move to Good to Firm, a flat track and no pace rival are all positives for a horse stepping up to a mile from a position of complete tactical control.
runners_data.comment: Fourth on her opening start at Yarmouth, beaten three lengths, Kino Plasmat left enough in hand to suggest there is clear scope for progress, and the longer trip here looks well suited to her; she rates a genuine threat to make that step forward.

races.paceDynamic: Kino Plasmat is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner maiden and, ridden by Cieren Fallon, is expected to stride straight to the front and control the pace without any meaningful challenge from the remainder of the field. Dark Whisper and Next Guilian are the only prominent types, but neither carries the profile to pressure Kino Plasmat for early supremacy, meaning the pace is likely to be measured rather than searching on this Good to Firm Ffos Las surface. From halfway the question becomes whether Kino Plasmat has enough left to repel the hold-up horses — Lean d'Aislingean and Elenaya — who will be hunting off the steady gallop from the rear. This race shape — a lone, uncontested lead dictating a controlled tempo on a flat, right-handed galloping track — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or at least quicken from a close-up position, as true hold-up runners may find the pace insufficient to generate the sustained sprint they need late on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kino Plasmat Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Kino Plasmat is allowed to bowl along in front at a controlled pace and the field never applies enough pressure to expose stamina limitations.
scenarios.body: If Kino Plasmat is allowed to bowl along in front at a controlled pace and the field never applies enough pressure to expose stamina limitations.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Chase Leader Down
scenarios.trigger: If Dark Whisper or Impierious press Kino Plasmat from the home turn and the acceleration of the front-runner is blunted by the sustained pursuit.
scenarios.body: If Dark Whisper or Impierious press Kino Plasmat from the home turn and the acceleration of the front-runner is blunted by the sustained pursuit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop quickens markedly in the final quarter-mile and creates enough of a true pace for the rear-division runners to close.
scenarios.body: If the gallop quickens markedly in the final quarter-mile and creates enough of a true pace for the rear-division runners to close.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Chaos Verdict
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace causes the entire field to bunch on the home turn and a tactical sprint develops over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If the steady pace causes the entire field to bunch on the home turn and a tactical sprint develops over the final two furlongs.

watchPoints.text: Kino Plasmat sets the tempo entirely alone — if Cieren Fallon is able to dictate an unchallenged lead into the straight, any horse not in a position to track or challenge early will be racing for minor honours only.

Next Guilian is flagged as a horse who fades in the finish; if it contests the early pace and weakens inside the final furlong it could impede hold-up runners like Lean d'Aislingean making late ground on the outside.

Elenaya returns from 192 days off the track with tongue-tie applied for the first time — monitor in the paddock and at the start for signs of ring-rustiness that could affect early positioning and therefore the shape of the race behind Kino Plasmat.

Vincenzo Bellini is a complete unknown on debut for a stable with a low recent strike rate; its drawn position and early behaviour in the stalls could alter the dynamic for the horses immediately around it, particularly the prominent-running Dark Whisper.

races.name: West Wales Properties Mayfair Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Angel's Call
runners_data.note: Disappointing recent form (fades in finish) and limited winning form on similar going; a natural hold-up horse who will be racing in a more forward position than ideal given the overcrowded rear, tempering expectations significantly.
runners_data.comment: Fourth here last time, beaten three lengths, Angel's Call has experience over the distance but is arguably better suited to shorter; he has been winless in his last five starts and first-time cheekpieces are the main hope of reversing that.

runners_data.name: A Rose Adaay
runners_data.note: Harry Vigors (5lb claimer) takes the ride for an in-form Grace Harris yard (1 from 15 last 14 days); stays 8f in good conditions but has been running primarily on soft ground and this quicker surface could be a key query.
runners_data.comment: Fifth at Chepstow latest, beaten five lengths, A Rose Adaay handles the distance and has claims off a reduced handicap mark; consistency has been lacking in recent form, however, and she needs to find more in this company.

runners_data.name: Belltony
runners_data.note: Richard Price has been quiet recently (0 from 2 last 14 days) and the horse's last win came on standside turf; although a genuine rear-of-field operator by instinct, the crowded hold-up contingent means it will likely be forced into a more central, less comfortable berth.
runners_data.comment: With experience at this mile trip and a fourth among recent efforts, Belltony looks capable of better than his recent finishes suggest and has genuine scope for improvement; he remains yet to score in his last four starts, which is the honest caveat.

runners_data.name: Blue Point Express
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle sends in with a 1/16 recent strike rate; goes in a hood and naturally wants to come from the back, but with the hold-up division oversubscribed, Edward Greatrex may elect to push forward earlier than the horse's form pattern suggests.
runners_data.comment: Beaten three-and-a-quarter lengths at Chepstow last time, Blue Point Express rates among the most interesting on our figures and first-time cheekpieces could spark a response; her form has been patchy and a more testing surface might bring out the best in her.

runners_data.name: King Of The Dance
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner for Bernard Llewellyn, who has a quiet 14-day record (0/6); the 7-year-old is proven over this course and distance on Good ground with 1W3P in similar conditions, and uncontested control from the front is his clear tactical advantage here.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in placing across a long run of recent starts, King Of The Dance handles ground conditions and the trip well, and first-time cheekpieces make him an interesting proposition; he has been beaten further than ideal lately and needs to convert those efforts into a result.

runners_data.name: Prince Ali
runners_data.note: Won last time out (1/8f/Soft) for Thomas Faulkner and arrives 24 days fresh; Zoe Lewis's 7lb claim is notable, and his hold-up style combined with solid placed form over this sort of trip makes him one of the better-credentialled closers in this field.
runners_data.comment: Prince Ali won at Chepstow last time by a neck and comes here in solid form, well suited to the distance; first-time cheekpieces are a new addition and he will need to settle to make the most of his clear advantages.

runners_data.name: Spirited Dancer
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane takes the mount for the Kubler yard (0/6 last 14 days); the 4-year-old has placed twice at 7f on Good ground recently and shows a consistent pattern of finishing into the money, making him a natural fit if the pace is sustainable.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up twice in her last three starts, including at Brighton last time, Spirited Dancer has found form on a consistent surface and appears to be on an upward curve; first-time cheekpieces add appeal, though she is arguably at her best over a shorter trip.

runners_data.name: Mokata
runners_data.note: Adam Kirby's yard is in form (2/12 last 14 days) and the 3-year-old carries the minimum 126lbs with a tongue-tie; however, it fades consistently in the finish and its entire recent form has come over longer trips on Good ground — the step back in distance is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Down the field at Brighton in a classified race last time, Mokata has struggled for consistency in recent starts but has yet to show her best over this distance; first-time cheekpieces are a new addition and could help her put in a better showing.

runners_data.name: Snow Day
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll is firing in winners (9/44 last 14 days) but this horse has very modest form, carrying an OR of just 35 and showing nothing better than an 8th in its last four starts; finishes are weak and it will need a completely different race scenario to feature.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in her last four starts, Snow Day is bottom-rated in this field and faces a stiff task; an eighth at Bath last time was a marginal improvement on previous outings, and her pedigree suggests the mile trip is at least not against her.

races.paceDynamic: King Of The Dance is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 9-runner 7½f Ffos Las classified stakes and, with no genuine rival to push him from the outside, he is likely to control proceedings from the front at a sustainable, owner-dictated tempo on Good to Firm ground. The field is saturated with hold-up types — Angel's Call, Belltony, Blue Point Express, Mokata and Snow Day are all natural rear-runners who cannot all find their preferred berth and have been redistributed to midfield on the pace map; of these, Blue Point Express and Belltony have the most realistic claims to actually securing a prominent position given their recent race patterns. With one uncontested pace-setter and a field full of closers who must traffic through each other, the race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or just off the leader in the slipstream, as the moderate tempo will not generate the strong late sectionals that true hold-up horses need to pounce.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: King Leads, Controls
scenarios.trigger: If King Of The Dance bowls along uncontested and sets a comfortable, gallop-controlling tempo from the outset.
scenarios.body: If King Of The Dance bowls along uncontested and sets a comfortable, gallop-controlling tempo from the outset.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a hold-up type manages to track King Of The Dance in second or third and gets a clean passage to challenge in the straight.
scenarios.body: If a hold-up type manages to track King Of The Dance in second or third and gets a clean passage to challenge in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Late
scenarios.trigger: If King Of The Dance goes off faster than expected and ties up inside the final two furlongs, opening the door for a late surge.
scenarios.body: If King Of The Dance goes off faster than expected and ties up inside the final two furlongs, opening the door for a late surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scrimmage, Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If the congested midfield causes interference or checking, scrambling the race shape entirely and opening a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: If the congested midfield causes interference or checking, scrambling the race shape entirely and opening a sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: King Of The Dance (Cieren Fallon) — if he gets a clean break and immediately establishes a 2-3 length advantage, he may never be headed; watch his jumping tactics at the start as uncontested control is his entire race.

Prince Ali (Zoe Lewis) — a winner last time and arriving fresh at 24 days, but Lewis's 7lb claim brings her out to 135lbs and traffic among the redistributed midfield pack could cost him the clear run he needs late.

Spirited Dancer (Billy Loughnane) — recent placed form at 7f on Good ground is directly relevant, but the Kubler yard is cold at 0/6 over 14 days; watch where Loughnane positions him in the opening two furlongs relative to King Of The Dance.

Blue Point Express and Belltony — both are natural rear-runners forced into an unfamiliar midfield role by the overcrowded hold-up division; if either is restless or unbalanced in the first half-mile, they become interference risks for the rest of the field.

Snow Day (Gina Mangan, Tony Carroll) — despite Carroll's hot yard form, this runner's OR of 35 and consistent fading patterns mean it is primarily a watch point for any impact it has on the traffic behind King Of The Dance in the early stages.

races.name: WWP 34 Years Finding Customers Their Dream Homes Handicap

runners_data.name: Dappled Light
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Adrian Wintle who arrives in career-best form having won back-to-back on good ground over a mile; the drop to 7½f and similar conditions look ideal, and 17 days between runs keeps him fresh — the hg:p headgear flag confirms he races up with the pace naturally.
runners_data.comment: In excellent form following back-to-back wins, most recently taking a handicap by a head at Bath off a 3lb lower mark, he now tries first-time cheekpieces on a stiffer rating; the trip and ground suit well enough.

runners_data.name: Sofian
runners_data.note: Lightly campaigned hold-up type trained by Nikki Evans, last seen 105 days ago, but that seasonal break coincides with a sharp return to good-to-firm conditions in which he won over a mile at Goodwood; 7½f looks on the short side for his most effective style and the long layoff is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: A 105-day absence follows a 10-length defeat at Wolverhampton, where he fell away sharply after showing better form before that; an unforgiving handicap mark and the need to recapture earlier promise make this a difficult ask on his comeback.

runners_data.name: Cypriot Diaspora
runners_data.note: Rod Millman hold-up runner whose last six outings have returned modest efforts ranging from fifth to ninth; sim-going figures of 1W1P from 15 are uninspiring, and against horses with stronger profiles this shape offers him little tactical advantage.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 10 lengths at Leicester last time, her form has declined markedly in recent starts; the official rating sits well below her last competitive level, but she would need to show considerable improvement to feature here.

runners_data.name: Tonal
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Ian Williams ridden by the in-form Billy Loughnane, who has won five times in the last 14 days for the stable overall; Tonal has won on artificial and handled good-to-firm ground in the past, and a 48-day freshener after a bold run suits his type — sits perfectly on the pace for this shape.
runners_data.comment: Down the field at Yarmouth on his most recent start, he had won twice in his last five starts; first-time cheekpieces applied here and he has made notable all-weather strides, suggesting the current mark could be workable.

runners_data.name: Arnaz
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane handler sends this horse fresh after 42 days, but Arnaz is at heart a hold-up runner that has been pushed into a midfield slot on the map because hold-up positions are already oversubscribed in this field; the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 signals it is likely to race out of its comfort zone, and tp headgear does not change the structural disadvantage here.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Lingfield last time after running too freely, he now wears a first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces; effective over six and seven furlongs on most surfaces, but the poor recent record makes him tough to recommend at this stage.

runners_data.name: Kaleidoscope Eyes
runners_data.note: Bernard Llewellyn's 4-year-old prominent type with a 7lb claimer in Zoe Lewis aboard, whose best form (a Haydock win over 8f on heavy) came on very different ground; the sim-going record of 0W0P from three good-ground starts is a red flag on today's surface.
runners_data.comment: Beaten eight lengths at Chepstow last time, her form has been inconsistent lately despite winning earlier in the year; she handles the trip and ground, but a string of modest recent runs makes it hard to back her with confidence.

runners_data.name: Medyg
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity for Edward Smyth-Osbourne as a lightly-raced 3-year-old stepping up from six furlongs; only four career starts and a sim-going record of 0W0P from a single comparable outing means the style tag of U (unknown) reflects real uncertainty, and the 57-day absence adds another layer of unpredictability.
runners_data.comment: Beaten four and a half lengths at Windsor on his last outing in a performance in keeping with recent level, he returns after a short break over a trip where settling will be important; capable enough but needs more here.

runners_data.name: Quilt
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, and Cieren Fallon's booking for Ed Walker is significant; Quilt's form string shows consistency at 7f on varying surfaces and his ability to dictate unopposed on today's good-to-firm ground is the single biggest shaper of this race's outcome — he is the pacesetter the whole field is drawn around.
runners_data.comment: Beaten eight lengths at Wolverhampton last time in a modest dip of form, she is bred for this sort of distance and has placed on several occasions in recent starts; must learn to relax to show her best, but earlier form warrants respect.

runners_data.name: Red Moon
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's 3-year-old hold-up type who is lightly weighted at 130lbs and comes in fresh after just 13 days; a win on good ground at Brighton over 7f gives genuine sim-going credentials, and if the pace truly collapses he is one of the better-credentialled finishers, though the structural race shape works against him.
runners_data.comment: Took a handicap by half a length at Salisbury two starts ago, then followed that with a placed effort last time off a mark just below today's; speedily bred and effective at this trip, he escapes a penalty and holds strong claims.

races.paceDynamic: Quilt is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no other horse genuinely competing for the lead, Cieren Fallon should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on good-to-firm ground at Ffos Las over seven-and-a-half furlongs. Behind him, Dappled Light and Tonal are the likely prominent stalkers, sitting just off the pace and ready to challenge if Quilt's fractions slacken, while Arnaz is a natural hold-up type who has been redistributed into a midfield slot on the map — the field carries more pace than the rear can accommodate, and Arnaz is unlikely to secure its preferred deep position. The uncontested, self-regulated tempo strongly favours prominent horses who can maintain their position throughout and pounce when Quilt is asked a question in the final two furlongs; hold-up horses relying on a fast-finishing end-to-end gallop are at a structural disadvantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Quilt Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Quilt sets an uncontested, measured pace and the prominent pair close efficiently from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: If Quilt sets an uncontested, measured pace and the prominent pair close efficiently from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Quilt Gallops Rivals Flat
scenarios.trigger: If Quilt quickens the tempo significantly in the back straight and the field cannot close from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: If Quilt quickens the tempo significantly in the back straight and the field cannot close from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Late Surge

watchPoints.text: Quilt's early fractions are the race-shaping variable — if Fallon eases him out of the gate and finds a comfortable rhythm unchallenged, the race could be over as a contest by the two-furlong pole; watch the opening two furlongs carefully.

Dappled Light's back-to-back winning form and identical conditions to today make him the most dangerous stalker; if he tracks Quilt within a length through the early stages, Tonal may be squeezed for the crucial second position off the pace.

Arnaz is a natural hold-up horse likely to be racing out of role in a field with limited deep space at the rear; if he is shuffled wide or forced to race too prominently, his STYLE_FIT penalty makes him vulnerable and potentially a drifter in running.

Red Moon's light weight of 130lbs and recent course-and-distance form give him each-way appeal if the pace slackens late, but he needs a genuine end-to-end gallop that the lone front-runner scenario rarely produces — monitor whether Quilt is allowed to coast.

Billy Loughnane's five wins in 14 days for Ian Williams is a stat worth tracking; if Tonal is sent forward early under Loughnane and disputes the pace with Quilt, the entire race shape flips toward a contested scenario — watch the early positioning of both horses from the stalls.

races.name: West Wales Properties Carmarthenshire Handicap

runners_data.name: Runamara
runners_data.note: Consistent enough hold-up filly for John & Rhys Flint with five runs showing a best of second over 6f on standard, but 5/12 form in similar going and no wins or placed efforts at this shorter 5f trip make the drop in distance a concern — Taylor Fisher in the saddle with 15 days since last run|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten last time in a handicap at Windsor, he remains without a win in recent starts and has shown only moderate form over six furlongs; the easing mark offers some hope, but significantly more is needed to trouble the principals here.

runners_data.name: Forever Glamorous
runners_data.note: Christopher Mason's filly has headgear (p) fitted and arrives with a solid recent run of three placings in five outings including a second over 6f on good; Gina Mangan takes the ride and the hold-up style in a pace-less race means she may be forced wider than ideal, though her 5f placed form on heavy gives hope she handles pace-less sprints|
runners_data.comment: Equipped with first-time cheekpieces for a trainer in good current form, he has been consistent over five and six furlongs on surfaces he handles well; a six-length Bath reverse last time was a dip, but the overall record makes him a genuine threat.

runners_data.name: Kodi K
runners_data.note: John Gallagher's three-year-old holds a natural deep hold-up style but the map has him positioned in midfield simply because the rear is oversubscribed — his genuine racing position is at the back, so his chance is tempered in a compressed sprint where getting there from that position is difficult; recent second over 5f good is the strongest form reference|
runners_data.comment: An improved effort last time, where he finished second beaten two lengths off a 2lb higher mark at Lingfield, suggests further progress is possible; effective over six furlongs, though he may require softer ground to show his best.

runners_data.name: Magnificent Mel
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's horse has posted two seconds in his last six and shows a pattern of running into places without winning — his true racing style is hold-up yet he fills a midfield slot on the map by necessity; six runs in similar going with 0W2P suggests he performs but cannot convert, and the 12-day turnaround is fine|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Lingfield on her most recent outing, she has nonetheless placed on several occasions over five and six furlongs, acts on good ground and the all-weather, and a return to those placed efforts could see her competitive here.

runners_data.name: My Mate Mackley
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on soft 24 days ago for Adam Kirby and carries that in-form stamp into this race; Billy Loughnane takes over in the saddle and headgear (p) is noted — his natural preference is to race from the rear but the map places him in midfield out of necessity, and his 5f winning form is the most relevant recent evidence in the field|
runners_data.comment: Fitted with first-time cheekpieces, he won by a nose at Chepstow on his penultimate start and backed that up with a placed effort last time on the same mark; effective over five and six furlongs, he looks to have a reasonable chance at these weights.

runners_data.name: Follow My Heart
runners_data.note: The second Rod Millman runner, partnered by Cieren Fallon, brings a poor recent form string of 95946 and only one run in similar going with no wins or places; he is a genuine hold-up type squeezed into a midfield role on the map and his limited scope for improvement on current evidence makes him the most vulnerable in this field|
runners_data.comment: Beaten over eight lengths at Salisbury last time in a performance consistent with her recent level, her pedigree is geared to shorter trips and she should improve for that outing; a workmanlike sort with limited recent form, she faces stiff competition here.

runners_data.name: Tanaka
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's runner arrives freshest of the field at just 7 days since his last run and has a win over 5f good in his recent history as well as consistent 5f form — Rob Hornby is a significant booking; tagged as a hold-up type mapped to midfield, his actual 5f good-ground winning form is the standout piece of evidence and he is the one whose profile fits this sprint-finish scenario most naturally|
runners_data.comment: In good form, she took a five-furlong handicap by a nose off the same mark at Beverley last time; now equipped with a first-time hood, her profile suggests there may be more to offer at this trip than her wider record implies.

races.paceDynamic: This 5f handicap at Ffos Las on Good to Firm ground has no confirmed front-runner in the field — every single runner carries a hold-up profile, meaning the race is almost certain to develop into a slow-burn sprint with a late dash rather than a genuine contested gallop from the gates. With no horse willing to commit early, the pace is likely to be modest through the early furlongs before the field fans out and sprints for home in the final two furlongs, creating a race that should theoretically suit horses with a sharp turn of foot from off the pace. However, the field holds far more genuine hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Magnificent Mel, Kodi K, My Mate Mackley, Follow My Heart, and Tanaka are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map simply because someone must fill those positions. The tactical verdict is clear: whoever can best exploit a compressed, moderate-pace scenario — likely those drawn or positioned to get a clean run in the straight — will hold the edge, and horses with proven 5f form on good ground such as Tanaka and My Mate Mackley are the style profiles most likely to capitalise on a sprint-finish shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch Tanaka's draw and early positioning — Rob Hornby on the only proven 5f good-ground winner in the field is the key market mover to track as stalls open|
With every runner a hold-up type, watch for a slow early pace that creates a convoy effect — if no horse commits forward in the first furlong, the bunching risk in the straight is severe|

My Mate Mackley won last time over this exact 5f trip but in soft ground — monitor whether the step up to Good to Firm blunts his finishing effort, as ground softness may have been a significant factor in that win|

Forever Glamorous and My Mate Mackley both carry headgear (p) — watch to see whether either breaks more sharply than expected and accidentally assumes the role of accidental front-runner in this pace-free race|

Rod Millman's double booking of Magnificent Mel and Follow My Heart warrants attention — trainer has 0/15 over the past 14 days and neither horse is filling their natural role in this race shape, so treat both with significant caution|

races.name: West Wales Properties Ceredigion Handicap

runners_data.name: Bulldog Spirit
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer whose recent form includes a win over 15f on Good going; Cieren Fallon in the saddle is a major positive, and the 2m trip with six-furlong stamina reserves on fast ground suits — Bernard Llewellyn's yard has struggled for form (0/6 T14) but this horse's sim-going record (1W2P) is encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and consistent in defeat, he was beaten three lengths from a 2lb higher mark last time, suggesting the current rating remains stiff; handles the trip and ground well enough to fill a place.

runners_data.name: Merrijig
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old who won over 16f on Standard last time and has placed three times on similar going; Gina Mangan takes the ride and the headgear (blinkers) is retained — the 22-day turnaround is fine, though John Berry's stable is quiet at 0/5 over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Fitted with first-time blinkers, he returned to form with a win two starts back and confirmed that with a 7l third at Pontefract most recently; handles the trip and remains on a manageable mark.

runners_data.name: Oakley
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner and structurally pivotal; the 275-day absence is the single biggest risk flag and this is a horse racing slightly out of its OR comfort zone, but an excellent sim-going record (3W9P from 12 starts on Good) and a sympathetic gallop with no rivals to press him make this a serious shape contender if fit.
runners_data.comment: Progressive over hurdles, he landed a handicap by half a length off a mark significantly above today's at Uttoxeter last time; effective at two miles on good ground, and Irish handicap experience adds further substance to the profile.

runners_data.name: Golden Flame
runners_data.note: A long-absentee (264 days) who has struggled on artificial surfaces; the 7lb claimer Zoe Lewis rides and the horse's best sim-going return is modest (0W2P from 3), while form over shorter trips on Soft last time adds a stamina-on-fast-ground question mark.
runners_data.comment: Returning from a 264-day absence, his finishing efforts late in races are a genuine strength, and he was beaten four lengths off this exact mark at Bath last time stepping back up in trip; handles the distance and going well, though freshness remains the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Simiyann
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map position because the rear is oversubscribed — Ian Williams has sent out five winners in the last 14 days (5/28) and Billy Loughnane is a high-quality booking, but the visor and a form string of 34-600 suggest this horse is struggling to find its best; sim-going record of 2W2P is reasonable though.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in the rear in his last two outings, he tries a first-time visor here; the official mark has eased, which offers some hope, but a significant step forward is needed to trouble the leading rivals.

runners_data.name: Chillhi
runners_data.note: Drops significantly in OR and wears tongue-tie and blinkers; the horse's natural race position is at the rear but will be forced forward by the traffic — a 64-day break with seven-day jockey change adds uncertainty, and its Good going record in similar races is moderate (2W3P from 9).
runners_data.comment: Fitted with a first-time tongue-tie and blinkers, he was pulled up at Newton Abbot last time in a hurdle contest and has shown erratic form of late; there is ability here on older evidence and the mark leaves room, but a return to form is needed.

runners_data.name: Cogital
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old veteran who has won recently over 17f on Good going and placed twice on similar surfaces (2W3P sim-going); the 61-day absence with a long jockey layoff is a concern, but Bernard Llewellyn knows this horse well and at OR 52 carries very low weight — naturally a hold-up type who won't get to the back of the field here.
runners_data.comment: A promising return to form over hurdles last time off a mark 35lb higher than today's raises genuine interest; he handles this trip on a sound surface and looks well treated if that form transfers to the flat.

runners_data.name: Sapphire Sirocco
runners_data.note: Won last time out (16f, Standard) and has a win on Good ground over the same trip; the 17-day turnaround is sharp and fresh, Barry John Murphy's yard sent out a winner recently (1/9 T14), and Ryan Kavanagh's 5lb claim helps on OR 50 — though like other closers in this field, will be closer to the pace than preferred.
runners_data.comment: In good form, she landed a handicap by a head at Bath last time from a mark 2lb lower than today's; handles fast ground and the trip, and the current rating looks fair for a mare with two wins in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Adrian
runners_data.note: Bernard Llewellyn's second string on the day; wears blinkers and has placed twice on Soft over 12f but has repeatedly failed on Standard surfaces — the 26-day break is routine, yet a form string of 308-62 and zero wins on sim-going (0W1P) dampen enthusiasm despite being pushed forward by traffic.
runners_data.comment: Fitted with first-time blinkers, he has competed at Group level in Germany and stays the full two miles; an encouraging second by a neck in a classified race here last time is a positive, but he remains without a win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Oceanides
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old flagged for fading in finishes, which is a material concern over 2m on fast ground; form of 9686 is consistently poor, no sim-going win or place recorded, and Olivia Tubb's 5lb claim may not compensate — this horse is a structural danger to itself more than the field.
runners_data.comment: Held comfortably in a classified race here last time, she makes her handicap debut over a longer trip which should suit given her middle-distance breeding; the step up is a positive, but she remains unexposed against more seasoned rivals.

runners_data.name: Marinakis
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner; no race-day relevance, though if reinstated at declaration stage the tongue-tie, moderate form on fast ground (0W0P sim-going) and recent poor finishes (334688) would make it one of the weaker propositions in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Oakley is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 2m handicap on Good to Firm ground at Ffos Las, and with no genuine rival to press him from the outset, he is set to control proceedings at a measured, sustainable gallop from the front. The rest of the field is dominated by hold-up types — Bulldog Spirit, Merrijig, Golden Flame, Simiyann, Chillhi, Cogital, Sapphire Sirocco, Adrian, Oceanides and Marinakis all want to race off the pace — meaning Oakley will not be harassed early and can dictate the tempo entirely on his own terms. This field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Simiyann, Chillhi, Cogital, Sapphire Sirocco and Adrian are all true closers who will be forced to race closer to the pace than is natural for them, compressing the field and reducing the ground they can make up in the straight. A controlled, front-runner-favoured tempo over this flat 2m trip on fast ground is the dominant shape, and the tactical verdict is clear: horses able to travel prominently or sit just off the lone leader — and see out the trip on this going — hold the structural advantage, while genuine deep closers face a race run at a pace that may never truly string them out.

watchPoints.text: Oakley's 275-day absence is the single most important swing factor in this race — if he shows any sign of greenness or blowing up on the way to post, the entire front-runner scenario collapses and the compressed closer pack becomes far more dangerous than the probabilities suggest.

The volume of hold-up horses forced closer to the pace than natural (Simiyann, Chillhi, Cogital, Sapphire Sirocco, Adrian) creates a risk of early jostling and a tighter early gallop than Oakley's presence alone would imply — watch for crowding on the first bend.

Sapphire Sirocco won last time and arrives on a sharp 17-day turnaround; if this horse travels fluently in mid-division rather than being squeezed wide early, its closing speed on Good to Firm ground makes it the most dangerous late runner to Oakley's scenario.

Billy Loughnane on Simiyann is a jockey well above the level of this race — if the visor sharpens the horse's early focus and it secures a better position than expected, its Ian Williams trainer form (5/28 over 14 days) makes it worth tracking through the race.

Oceanides is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — over 2m on quick ground as a 4-year-old, watch for it weakening at the top of the straight and potentially causing interference for horses making their runs from midfield.
